title: Farm Solar Array: full outage (2024-02-05 to 2024-02-06)
summary: Full outage detected at Farm Solar Array (Arbuckle, CA) over 2 day(s), 2024-02-05 to 2024-02-06. Estimated cost so far: $540.
evidence: Performance index fell from 0.98 in the two weeks before to a median of 0.00 during the event (1.00 = healthy).
Estimated energy lost: 4,504 kWh (100% of expected), about $540.
likely_causes: Inverter trip (ground fault, over-temperature, grid event)
recommended_actions: Check SCADA / inverter alarm log for the trip code and time of the first fault
Confirm grid availability with the utility before dispatch (rule out a feeder outage)
If alarms allow, attempt one remote reset; otherwise dispatch a technician
On site: inspect inverter, AC disconnect and breakers; follow lockout/tagout
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: Farm Solar Array: partial outage (2024-03-31 to 2024-04-15)
summary: Partial outage detected at Farm Solar Array (Arbuckle, CA) over 16 day(s), 2024-03-31 to 2024-04-15. Estimated cost so far: $2,282.
evidence: Performance index fell from 0.99 in the two weeks before to a median of 0.75 during the event (1.00 = healthy).
Estimated energy lost: 19,018 kWh (25% of expected), about $2,282.
Roughly 26% of capacity appears offline, from the size of the step.
Performance stepped down abruptly and stayed flat, the signature of a share of the array going offline (an inverter, a combiner or a string).
likely_causes: One inverter or inverter module offline
Tripped DC disconnect in one block
recommended_actions: Compare inverter- and combiner-level currents to locate the offline section
Pull inverter fault logs for the start date
Inspect combiner-box fuses and string connectors in the affected block
Run IV-curve traces on suspect strings; replace failed fuses or components
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: Farm Solar Array: soiling / gradual loss (2024-07-02 to 2024-08-08)
summary: Soiling / gradual loss detected at Farm Solar Array (Arbuckle, CA) over 38 day(s), 2024-07-02 to 2024-08-08. Estimated cost so far: $2,636.
evidence: Performance index fell from 0.97 in the two weeks before to a median of 0.88 during the event (1.00 = healthy).
Estimated energy lost: 21,965 kWh (13% of expected), about $2,636.
The decline appears to have started around 2024-06-12, 20 days before it crossed the alert threshold.
Performance recovered to 0.99 of baseline in the week after.
A slow, steady slide in performance with no sudden step, the signature of dust or pollen build-up (or gradual degradation), followed by a sharp recovery consistent with rain or cleaning.
likely_causes: Dust or pollen build-up during a dry spell
recommended_actions: Visually inspect a sample of modules and photograph the soiling
Compare against the decline start date and the last rain or wash
Schedule a wash if the recoverable energy outweighs the cleaning cost; check the rain forecast first
After cleaning, confirm the performance index returns to its baseline
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: Farm Solar Array: irradiance sensor fault (2024-09-02 to 2024-09-22)
summary: Irradiance sensor fault detected at Farm Solar Array (Arbuckle, CA) over 21 day(s), 2024-09-02 to 2024-09-22.
evidence: Performance index fell from 0.99 in the two weeks before to a median of 1.14 during the event (1.00 = healthy).
Output is above what the measured irradiance allows, so the irradiance sensor is most likely reading low (dirty, drifting or misaligned).
recommended_actions: Clean the plane-of-array pyranometer and check its level and tilt alignment
Cross-check its readings against a second on-site sensor or satellite irradiance
Recalibrate or replace the sensor if the offset persists
Treat performance numbers for this window as unreliable until fixed
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: Farm Solar Array: curtailment / output cap (2024-10-26 to 2024-10-29)
summary: Curtailment / output cap detected at Farm Solar Array (Arbuckle, CA) over 4 day(s), 2024-10-26 to 2024-10-29. Estimated cost so far: $191.
evidence: Performance index fell from 0.98 in the two weeks before to a median of 0.85 during the event (1.00 = healthy).
Estimated energy lost: 1,593 kWh (13% of expected), about $191.
Midday output ran 19 points further below expectation than morning and evening output.
Output matches expectation in the morning and evening but is capped at midday on sunny days, which points to an export limit or inverter power setpoint rather than lost capacity.
likely_causes: Inverter clipping from an incorrect AC rating setting
recommended_actions: Ask the utility whether an export limit or curtailment order was in effect
Check the plant controller and inverter active-power limit setpoints
If no limit was ordered, restore the setpoint and document the change
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.

title: Farm Solar Array: monitoring data gap (2024-11-21 to 2024-11-23)
summary: Monitoring data gap detected at Farm Solar Array (Arbuckle, CA) over 3 day(s), 2024-11-21 to 2024-11-23.
evidence: No meter readings during daylight; output during this window is unknown.
recommended_actions: Check data-logger power and network/modem connectivity
Back-fill the gap from inverter internal logs or the revenue meter
Confirm the site was producing during the gap (meter totals)
safety_notes: Follow site lockout/tagout and arc-flash procedures before opening any DC or AC enclosure.
